podcast.body: The first single from "Paul's Boutique," released on July 25th, 1989. This track showcased the album's advanced sampling techniques, incorporating snippets from 16 different songs. The song's most obvious sample is a line from The Sweet's "Ballroom Blitz," and its title is derived from Curtis Blow's "Party Time." Other notable samples include material from James Brown, The Commodores, Kool & the Gang, and Edwin Starr, demonstrating a staggering complexity of mixing samples with original music. "Sixteen different songs are rated for this track."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was the first single released from the Beastie Boys' second album, *Paul's Boutique*. It marked a significant stylistic change from their earlier work, moving away from the "frat boy goofiness" and "big guitars." The track meticulously incorporated samples from 16 different songs, including a line from The Sweet's "Ballroom Blitz," with the song's title derived from Curtis Blow's "Party Time." Additionally, snippets from James Brown, The Commodores, Kool & The Gang, and Edwin Starr can be heard. The complexity of this mix of samples and original music was considered "staggering for its day." "Sixteen different songs are rated for this track."
